title: Compatogram: call-fingerprint and invocation envelope for OpenAI ↔ Legacy function compatibility
creator: Priya Kumar
description: Introduce the 'compatogram' layer: a deterministic translation layer that normalizes OpenAI-style tool descriptors and legacy function metadata into a compact call-fingerprint and an invocation envelope that the runtime can route, stream, and validate. This ticket captures design decisions, implementation plan, tests, and rollout for supporting streaming partial tool responses, structured JSON outputs, name-aliasing, and backwards-compatible fallbacks for legacy function payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts requests with either OpenAI-style 'tools' or legacy 'function' field and produces identical invocation envelopes downstream.
Streaming tool responses preserve provenance markers and can interleave partial structured outputs (JSON fragments) without breaking existing consumer SDKs.
Name normalization maps a configurable alias table; conflicts are logged and surfaced via the Console rollout page.
Fallback policy: when a tool name collision occurs, the compatogram applies deterministic call-fingerprint precedence and records telemetry for user migration nudges.
All changes covered by unit/integration tests and a staged rollout to ~10% of traffic in runtime-2.3 release.
Security review completed for invocation provenance headers and no PII leakage paths introduced.
decisions: Use a stable SHA256-based call-fingerprint generated from canonicalized (name, input-schema, version) to route requests reliably across deployments.
Do not alter user-visible tool names in API responses; present normalized metadata separately in headers/event-metadata to avoid breaking clients.

Streaming model -> tool call bridge will emit three event types: invocation.start, invocation.chunk (may contain JSON fragment or text), invocation.end. Each event includes 'cf' (call-fingerprint) and 'prov_id' (invocation provenance id).

Prefer schema-first validation for structured outputs via embedded JSON-Schema in the invocation envelope. If validation fails, emit structured 'schema_error' event and continue with best-effort fallback unless strict mode is enabled.
Backwards compatibility: legacy 'functions' without version or schema will be treated as 'legacy-mode' with heuristics and assigned a synthetic call-fingerprint with 'legacy:true' tag.
Telemetry: record counts of aliasing, collisions, schema failures, streaming reorders, and fallback invocations for product analytics and migration docs.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API surface): Parser that accepts both OpenAI 'tools' and legacy 'function' shapes; produces canonical tool descriptor and call-fingerprint.
Phase 2 (Runtime): Extend invoker to attach 'cf' and 'prov_id' to streaming events and to maintain per-invocation KV for structured-output reassembly.
Phase 3 (Console): Expose alias table UI and conflict alerts in Console rollouts + per-route diagnostics for call-fingerprint mismatches.
Phase 4 (SDKs): Small SDK patch to expose invocation events and a helper to reassemble structured outputs across streaming chunks (non-breaking; fall back to previous behavior if not used).
Phase 5 (Rollout): Canary in runtime-2.3 -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> full, with metrics gating on error rate, schema failures, and latency regressions.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Priya Kumar: Initial spec drafted and shared in #infra-interop; linked Confluence and initial proto for call-fingerprint.
2026-03-03 - Marissa Chen (review): Asked for explicit guarantees around stream ordering and guidance for SDK behavior when chunks arrive out of order. Recommended prov_id to be RFC4122 UUIDv4.

2026-03-05 - Liam O'Connor: Implementation spike completed. Prototype stores partial JSON fragments in per-invocation KV and reassembles on invocation.end. Found edge case where model emits closing brace in separate chunk; added tolerant parser and test cases.

2026-03-07 - Diego Ramos (security): Flagged need to redact API keys in any logged invocation metadata. Added requirement: redact-sensitive=true for any console logs or telemetry fields containing user payloads.
2026-03-09 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 (compatogram parser + streaming event envelope).
2026-03-10 - QA: Integration test harness added to repo: tests/compatogram/test_stream_reassembly.py; initial run passing on dev cluster.
tests: Unit: canonicalizer_unit_test.py covers name normalization, fingerprint stability across whitespace/order changes.
Integration: stream_reassembly_test validates JSON fragment reassembly and schema-first validation behavior.
E2E: run compatibility matrix against samples from 3 major OSS models + legacy function payloads to ensure identical invocation envelopes.
Load: synthetic workload that mixes short-chat + high-throughput embedding requests to validate no regression in tail latency when compatogram enabled.
rollout: Canary toggle under runtime feature-flag 'compatogram-v1' deployed to a subset of pods.
Monitor SLOs: p95 latency, invocation.error_rate, schema.failure_rate, and telemetry cardinality for aliases.
If schema_failure_rate > 0.5% for 30m or invocation.error_rate increases > 0.3% absolute, rollback compatogram toggle.
Communication: Email to customers on Dedicated/Private tiers explaining alias behavior and Console migration guidance prior to full rollout.
